teaser.text: POP MART International Group Limited turns artist-created characters into collectibles, plush and experiences, then sells them through a network that reaches fans directly and through partners. Its business is simple to describe but not simple to assess: money arrives when a fan or reseller buys, and leaves through the costs of creating, making, moving and renewing the characters.

stock.opening: The weighted forecast is HKD158.73 in October 2027. It hinges on Pop Mart proving its next characters can carry growth as THE MONSTERS normalizes.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers what drives Pop Mart’s business, how its rivals compare, how management allocates capital and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could Pop Mart's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is HKD158.73 in October 2027, a +13% return. It reaches HKD224.00 in October 2029, a +63% return including dividends. The bear case carries 35% probability. Base is 45%; bull is 20%.

The last-date range runs from HKD68.65 in the bear case to HKD494.91 in the bull case. Today's price is HKD142.20. The base case is most likely at 45%. The bear case carries 35%, and the bull case 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Pop Mart, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Base earnings rise from CNY14,100 million in October 2027 to CNY16,655.296 million in October 2029. The forecast uses revenue growth that slows from an initially strong level and margins below 2025's 34.4%, because newer IPs can partly replace THE MONSTERS while overseas returns and inventory costs remain uneven. Bear earnings fall from CNY11,340 million to CNY11,031.6 million as the breakout fades. Bull earnings rise from CNY16,120 million to CNY24,760.32 million if new characters, overseas restocking and inventory normalization reinforce one another. Management has already said it would “highly probably” miss its 2026 growth target, which supports moderation rather than extrapolation.

The bull case needs new characters to become durable franchises, overseas stores to achieve better productivity, inventory to normalize and cash conversion to recover. It lifts the shares from HKD263.88 in 2027 to HKD494.91 in 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the number of conditions that must succeed together and the limited public store-cohort data.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Pop Mart really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow remained substantial after capital spending, lease payments and interest. But real free cash flow, after stock-based pay, represented a smaller share of revenue than it had in the prior year. In the six months ended 30 June 2026, free cash flow also fell from the comparable period even as profit continued to grow.

dividend.title: Pop Mart dividend: history, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: Pop Mart’s dividend history, cash coverage, buybacks, risks and yield, in plain English.
dividend.opening: Pop Mart’s latest annual dividend was CNY2.38 per share. Pop Mart generated RMB9,271.614 million of free cash flow in 2025, and dividends were a recurring use of cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also answers how Pop Mart makes money, how it compares with rivals, what management is doing, and which risks could change the story.

blocks.heading: How much does Pop Mart pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends grow from CNY2.40 to CNY2.80 per share in the base case, broadly preserving a payout near 25% of earnings. The bear case cuts DPS from CNY1.50 to CNY1.00 as cash conversion weakens. The bull case raises it from CNY3.00 to CNY4.60 as earnings and cash recover. The latest annual DPS was CNY2.38, but the company has given no dividend-growth target.

blocks.heading: Does Pop Mart’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left after the operating business and investment in fixed assets. It rose from RMB271.469 million in 2021 to RMB9,271.614 million in 2025. It is not money that can all be spent freely, because Pop Mart still needs cash for inventory, logistics, stores, and unexpected costs. Cash and short-term investments reached RMB17,234.752 million at year-end 2025.

Dividends were a recurring use of cash, while buybacks varied. The table records RMB634.31 million of buybacks in 2022. It records none in 2025. In the first half of 2026, Pop Mart paid RMB3,149,378,000 in dividends for the previous year and declared no interim dividend.

blocks.heading: What could change Pop Mart’s dividend?

paragraphs.text: The forecast would move toward the bear case if overseas weakness persists during 2027–2028, inventory turns slow and provisions rise, or character concentration remains high into 2028–2029. Those events would lower both earnings and the P/E.

blocks.heading: What is Pop Mart’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, says how much investors pay for each unit of profit. Free-cash-flow yield measures the cash left after operating and investment payments, while dividend yield measures only what the company distributes. Customers pay Pop Mart, and Pop Mart pays suppliers, employees, landlords and tax; the remainder can fund stores, product development, expansion, buybacks or dividends.
